say.en: Every enzyme in our body works best near 37 degrees Celsius and at a particular pH. Shift the temperature or pH and the reactions slow down. In this lesson: Explain the effects of temperature, pH and substrate concentration.
Describe competitive inhibition.
Name the six classes of enzymes and the three kinds of co-factors.

body.en: Each *enzyme* shows its highest activity at an optimum temperature and an optimum pH, with activity falling on either side. Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state, while high temperature destroys it because proteins are denatured by heat. As substrate concentration rises, the velocity rises at first and then reaches a maximum, Vmax, which is not exceeded because there are no free enzyme molecules left to bind more substrate. An inhibitor that closely resembles the substrate in molecular structure and competes for the active site is a competitive inhibitor; for example, malonate inhibits succinic dehydrogenase because it resembles the substrate succinate. Such inhibitors are often used to control bacterial pathogens.

points.en: Optimum temperature and pH give maximum *activity*.
Competitive inhibitor: substrate look-alike that blocks the active site.

narration.en: Warm the enzyme and substrate. The rate rises as molecules collide more often, roughly doubling every ten degrees, until about forty degrees. Above that the enzyme loses its shape, and its active site with it, and the rate falls steeply.

caption.en: Warming speeds up collisions between enzyme and substrate, so the rate rises (about doubling every 10 °C). Above about 45 °C the enzyme is denatured: its active site loses its shape and the rate falls steeply. The peak is the optimum temperature.
caption.kn: ಬಿಸಿಯಾದಂತೆ ಕಿಣ್ವ ಮತ್ತು ಆಧಾರ ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ಡಿಕ್ಕಿಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿ ದರ ಏರುತ್ತದೆ (ಪ್ರತಿ 10 °C ಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು ದ್ವಿಗುಣ). ಸುಮಾರು 45 °C ಮೇಲೆ ಕಿಣ್ವ ವಿಕೃತಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ: ಕ್ರಿಯಾಶೀಲ ತಾಣ ಆಕಾರ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಶಿಖರವೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ತಾಪಮಾನ.

say.en: Activity rises with temperature up to an optimum, then falls steeply as the enzyme is denatured. Low temperature only inactivates it.
Each enzyme also has an optimum pH: pepsin works in the acid stomach, trypsin in the alkaline intestine.
As substrate increases, the rate rises and then levels off at Vmax, when every enzyme molecule is busy. A competitive inhibitor slows the rise.
Enzymes fall into six classes. Many need a non-protein co-factor: a prosthetic group, a coenzyme or a metal ion.
Let us sketch how temperature, pH, substrate and inhibitors change the rate, then list the six classes.

body.en: *Enzymes* are divided into six classes: oxidoreductases/dehydrogenases (oxidation–reduction between two substrates), transferases (transfer a group other than hydrogen), hydrolases (hydrolyse ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic and other bonds), lyases (remove groups by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds), isomerases (inter-convert optical, geometric or positional isomers) and ligases (link two compounds, e.g. C–O, C–S, C–N, P–O bonds). Many enzymes need a non-protein co-factor; the protein part is then the apoenzyme. Prosthetic groups are tightly bound (haem in peroxidase and catalase); coenzymes are bound only transiently, and many contain vitamins (NAD and NADP contain niacin); some enzymes need metal ions, such as zinc for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase. Removing the co-factor destroys catalytic activity.

points.en: Six classes: Oxidoreductases, Transferases, Hydrolases, Lyases, Isomerases, Ligases.
Haem: prosthetic group; NAD: coenzyme; Zn²⁺: metal ion of carboxypeptidase.

problem.en: Classify each enzyme action: (a) a group other than hydrogen moves from one substrate to another; (b) a peptide bond is broken by adding water; (c) two molecules are joined using a C–N bond.

steps.en: (a) Transfer of a group other than hydrogen between substrates: transferase.
(b) Breaking a bond by adding water: hydrolase.

a Transfer of a group other than hydrogen between substrates: transferase.
b Breaking a bond by adding water: hydrolase.
c Linking two compounds together: ligase.
So the answer is a Transferase b Hydrolase c Ligase.

points.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಕಿಣ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ಅತ್ಯುತ್ತಮ ತಾಪ ಮತ್ತು pH ಇದೆ; ಅಧಿಕ ಶಾಖ ಅದನ್ನು ನಾಶ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Velocity reaches Vmax at high substrate concentration.
points.kn: ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಆಧಾರವಸ್ತು ಇದ್ದಾಗ ವೇಗ Vmax ತಲುಪುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate, e.g. malonate.
points.kn: ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾತ್ಮಕ ಪ್ರತಿಬಂಧಕಗಳು ಆಧಾರವಸ್ತುವನ್ನು ಹೋಲುತ್ತವೆ, ಉದಾ: ಮ್ಯಾಲೊನೇಟ್.

points.en: Six enzyme classes; co-factors: prosthetic groups, coenzymes, metal ions.
points.kn: ಆರು ಕಿಣ್ವ ವರ್ಗಗಳು; ಸಹಕಾರಕಗಳು ಮೂರು ವಿಧ.

homework.en: Draw the graph of enzyme velocity against substrate concentration and mark Vmax.

narration.en: Recap. Each enzyme has an optimum temperature and pH; heat denatures it. Velocity reaches Vmax at high substrate concentration. Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate, e.g. malonate. Six enzyme classes; co-factors: prosthetic groups, coenzymes, metal ions.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Each enzyme has an optimum temperature and pH; heat denatures it.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಕಿಣ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ಅತ್ಯುತ್ತಮ ತಾಪ ಮತ್ತು pH ಇದೆ; ಅಧಿಕ ಶಾಖ ಅದನ್ನು ನಾಶ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

say.kn: ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಆಧಾರವಸ್ತು ಇದ್ದಾಗ ವೇಗ Vmax ತಲುಪುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate, e.g. malonate.
say.kn: ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾತ್ಮಕ ಪ್ರತಿಬಂಧಕಗಳು ಆಧಾರವಸ್ತುವನ್ನು ಹೋಲುತ್ತವೆ, ಉದಾ: ಮ್ಯಾಲೊನೇಟ್.

say.en: Six enzyme classes; co-factors: prosthetic groups, coenzymes, metal ions.
say.kn: ಆರು ಕಿಣ್ವ ವರ್ಗಗಳು; ಸಹಕಾರಕಗಳು ಮೂರು ವಿಧ.
